defects: Specializes the base ring to k = ℂ specifically, whereas the gold statement holds for an arbitrary commutative ring k
Requires G and H to be Groups ([Group G] [Group H]), whereas gold only requires Monoid G, Monoid H — a stronger (narrower) hypothesis than the gold statement

'Representation H ℂ' is malformed: Mathlib's Representation takes three explicit type parameters (k, G, V), so this only supplies k and G and omits the underlying module/vector-space type V, meaning the term as written does not typecheck

Uses '.restrictScalars' to model restriction of a representation along a group homomorphism, but restrictScalars in Mathlib is the ring/scalar-restriction operation, not the correct operation for pulling back a representation along a monoid/group hom (which gold expresses via resFunctor); this conflates two distinct constructions

Uses ad hoc notation 'f →+[H] g' (suggestive of DistribMulActionHom) for morphisms between representations, which is not the actual morphism type in the Rep/Action category (k-linear G-equivariant maps), so it doesn't correspond to gold's categorical morphisms
The anonymous constructor '⟨α, β⟩' for ShortComplex omits the required proof that the composite is zero, so the short complex is not well-formed as stated

Restates the exactness equivalence via a universally quantified triple of representations and two maps rather than an actual ShortComplex object S and its image under a restriction functor (S.map (resFunctor f)) as in gold, changing the logical shape of the statement
Loses the universe generality (Rep.{w} k G) present in gold by fixing the representation category to ℂ-representations without the analogous universe parameter
